text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal and Lisbon world fair Expo 98 are negotiating an agreement under which TAP would be the official airline at the Expo.
- Electricity company EDP is to raise to 24 percent from 15 percent its stake in the capital of Sociedade Bioelectrica, which is building a combined cycle power plant in Pisa, Italy.
- By the end of 1996 there will be between 175,000 and 180,000 users of "paging" in Portugal, says Pereira da Costa, president of Telechamada.
- Banco Efisa is studying the possibility of launching an investment bank in Guinea-Bissau, the paper learned from a source close to the process.
- Portuguese police suspected of involvement in two suspicious deaths of young drug addicts in recent days.
- French truckers' strike harms Portuguese car industry. Auto-Europa and Opel factories in Palmela, south of Lisbon, are receiving supplies transported by air.
- Industry leaders in the pulp sector will deliver a study to Prime Minister Antonio Guterres today, urging the government to take steps to develop the country's forests.
- Portuguese textile industry is growing due to increasing consumption in Europe.
- Portuguese government will press the French government for compensation for losses incurred by Portuguese truck drivers as a result of the French truckers' strike.
